slot.brief: How many octahedral and tetrahedral voids per atom in fcc; 4 options with the correct count relationship.

stem: In a face-centred cubic (fcc) unit cell, the number of octahedral voids and tetrahedral voids per constituent atom are, respectively:
working: In an fcc unit cell, number of atoms Z = 4. Number of octahedral voids per unit cell = 4 (1 at body centre + 12 edge centres × 1/4 = 3, total 4). Number of tetrahedral voids per unit cell = 8. Therefore, per atom: octahedral voids = 4/4 = 1; tetrahedral voids = 8/4 = 2.
solution:
An fcc unit cell contains $Z=4$ atoms. It has $1+12\times\frac14=4$ octahedral voids and $8$ tetrahedral voids.
$$\text{Voids per atom}=\frac{4}{4},\;\frac{8}{4}=1,\;2$$
